extracted.intended_audience: computational number theorists and PARI/GP users computing with elliptic curves, p-adic heights, and L-functions
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of PARI/GP library routines for elliptic curves, p-adic heights, hyperelliptic routines and L-functions: definitions, calling conventions, expected outputs and mathematical normalizations to use when computing invariants and performing numerical experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical p-adic height normalization (reduction-dependent)
rubrics_metrics.description: When E has good ordinary reduction at p or non-split multiplicative reduction, the “canonical” p-adic height is obtained from ellpadicheight(E,p,n,P) by applying the linear change [1,-s2]^~ where s2 = ellpadics2(E,p,n). When E has split multiplicative reduction (Tate curve), the canonical height is obtained by multiplying ellpadicheight(E,p,n,P) by [1,-s2 + 1/log(q)/u2]~ where [u2,u,q] = Ep.tate and Ep = ellinit(E[1..5], O(p^(n))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: s2 does not depend on P, so compute it once with s2 = ellpadics2(E,p,n) and reuse it. Examples provided: using ellpadics2 then ellpadicheightmatrix* [1,-s2]~ to compute regulators; explicit example with E="5077a1", p=5, n=7. Normalizations chosen to make p-adic BSD statements easy.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicheightmatrix: Gram matrix of cyclotomic p-adic height
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a vector Q of points, ellpadicheightmatrix(E,p,n,Q) returns the 'Gram matrix' [F,G] of the cyclotomic p-adic height h_E with respect to the basis (ω,η) of D = H^1_dR(E) ⊗ Q Q_p to n p-adic digits. If ellpadicheight(E,p,n,Q[i],Q[j]) = [f,g] then F[i,j]=f and G[i,j]=g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The returned F and G are p-adic integral approximations (examples show lift(F) for readability). To get the canonical Gram matrix use [F,G] * [1,-ellpadics2(E,p,n)]~. Library syntax: ellpadicheightmatrix(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN Q).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadiclog: formal logarithm in kernel of reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E over K = Q or Q_p and P = [x,y] in the kernel of reduction mod p, let t(P) = -x/y be the formal group parameter; ellpadiclog(E,p,n,P) returns L(t) where L is the formal logarithm attached to the canonical invariant differential satisfying dL = dx/(2y + a1 x + a3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when P lies in kernel of reduction. Examples: ellpadiclog(E,2,10,P) and computations after finding suitable Q = ellmul(E,P,2). Library syntax: ellpadiclog(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN P).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadicregulator: p-adic regulator output and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: ellpadicregulator(E,p,n,S) returns the regulator R for E/Q and vector S=(S1,...,Sr) with respect to the canonical cyclotomic p-adic height, given to n p-adic digits. For ordinary reduction this is the determinant of the Gram matrix in Q_p; for supersingular reduction R is an element of D = H^1_dR(E) ⊗ Q Q_p (two-dimensional) and the function returns R in the basis (ω, F ω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation explains how to interpret R via the alternating bilinear form [.,.]_D with [ω,η]_D=1 and formulas [R,η]_D = det(h(S_i,S_j)_η) etc. Use ellpadicregulator(GEN E, GEN p, long n, GEN S). This normalization facilitates p-adic BSD formulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpadics2: slope of unit eigenvector of Frobenius (s2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For p>2 and E/Q with ordinary good reduction at p, ellpadics2(E,p,n) returns the slope s2 of the unit eigenvector of ellpadicfrobenius(E,p,n), i.e., the c ∈ p^{-1}Z_p such that η + s2 ω is an eigenvector for the unit eigenvalue of Frobenius on D_p(E) in the basis (ω,η=xω).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: s2 equals b2/12 - E2/12 where E2 is the Katz p-adic Eisenstein series; it is the unique c for which the odd solution σ(t)=t+O(t^2) of -d(1/σ dσ ω) = (x(t)+c)ω lies in tZ_p[[t]]. Compute s2 once and reuse when constructing canonical p-adic heights: h(E,p,n,P,s2) = ellpadicheight(E,[p,[1,-s2]],n,P). Library syntax: ellpadics2(GEN E, GEN p, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellperiods: normalized periods and optional quasi-periods
rubrics_metrics.description: ellperiods(w,{flag=0}) returns normalized periods [W1,W2] generating the same lattice as w so that τ=W1/W2 has positive imaginary part and lies in the standard fundamental domain for SL_2(Z). If flag=1 returns [[W1,W2],[η1,η2]] with quasi-periods η_i satisfying η2 W1 - η1 W2 = 2 i π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Output is intended to be used as first argument to ellwp, ellzeta, ellsigma. Quasi-periods are needed by ellzeta and ellsigma only. Library syntax: ellperiods(GEN w, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpointtoz: map point on E to complex/p-adic parameter z
rubrics_metrics.description: Given E/C (C/Λ) and P on E, ellpointtoz(E,P) computes z modulo the lattice Λ with P = [℘_Λ(z), ℘'_Λ(z)] (Weierstrass parametrization). Returns 0 for point at infinity. Behavior over R, number fields and Q_p depends on embeddings and reduction: for split multiplicative reduction returns φ(P) ∈ Q_p, for non-split returns a t_POLMOD in the unramified quadratic extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For E defined over R and P∈E(R) returned z lies in rectangle [0,w1)×[0,w2) as described. For p-adic Tate curves use E.tate to obtain [u2,u,q] and interpret outputs accordingly. Library syntax: zell(GEN E, GEN P, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellratpoints: enumerate affine rational points up to naive height
rubrics_metrics.description: ellratpoints(E,h,{flag=0}) returns a vector of affine rational points on integral model E with naive height less than h. If flag=1 stops as soon as a point is found and returns either empty vector or single point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: h can be specified as in hyperellratpoints (see hyperellratpoints for h formats). Example: ellratpoints(E,10) returns all points with naive height <10. Library syntax: ellratpoints(GEN E, GEN h, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellrootno: local and global root numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: ellrootno(E,{p}) computes the local root number of the L-series at place p (p=0 denotes infinite place). If p is omitted returns the global root number; in that case the curve can be over a number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global root number equals sign of functional equation and conjecturally parity of Mordell-Weil rank. Computation is faster if equation is minimal at p but not required. Library syntax: long ellrootno(GEN E, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsea: compute #E(F_q) using SEA with early-exit via tors argument
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsea(E,{tors=0}) computes the order of E(F_q) with the SEA algorithm. The tors argument allows early exit: if tors>0, returns 0 as soon as a small prime factor not dividing tors is detected. If tors is negative, similar checks apply to the quadratic twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set tors=1 to insist on prime order, tors=2 to allow a power-of-two cofactor, etc. Use ellsea to speed up searches for almost-prime order curves; for general cardinality use ellcard. Caveats: SEA not implemented for characteristic ≤7 or very small q (q ≤ 523), where ellcard is used; for field cardinality <~250 ellcard may be faster. ellsea does not store result in E. Recomended to install seadata package to speed up computation. Library syntax: ellsea(GEN E, long tors).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsearch: locate curves in elldata by name/conductor
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsearch(N) finds curves in elldata satisfying constraint N. N can be a string (curve name, isogeny class, conductor), a vector encoding same constraints, or an integer conductor. If N codes a full curve name outputs [N,[a1,a2,a3,a4,a6],G] with coefficients and Z-basis of free part of Mordell-Weil group; otherwise returns vector of matching curves in that format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ellsearchcurve(GEN N) when only complete curve names are accepted. Examples: ellsearch("11a3") or ellsearch([11,0,3]). Library syntax: ellsearch(GEN N).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsigma: Weierstrass sigma function and log(σ) determination
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsigma(L,{z=x},{flag=0}) computes σ(z,L) of the Weierstrass sigma function attached to lattice L (as given by ellperiods). The product/formula expansion is provided. If flag=1 computes an arbitrary determination of log(σ(z)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input L may be [ω1,ω2] or an ellinit structure (E.omega). Quasi-periods from ellperiods can be given for efficiency. Default series precision used if z omitted. Library syntax: ellsigma(GEN L, GEN z = NULL, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsub: difference of elliptic-curve points via parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: ellsub(E, z1, z2) computes the difference of the points corresponding to parameters z1 and z2 on the elliptic curve E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple wrapper/difference operation; library syntax GEN ellsub(GEN E, GEN z1, GEN z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltamagawa: compute global Tamagawa number including infinity
rubrics_metrics.description: elltamagawa(E) returns the global Tamagawa number of curve E (including factor at infinite places).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates computing local factors with elllocalred(e,p) then multiplying them, noting factor at infinity determined by sign of e.disc. Library syntax: GEN elltamagawa(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltaniyama: modular parametrization power series
rubrics_metrics.description: elltaniyama(E,{d=seriesprecision}) computes the modular parametrization Φ: X_0(N)→E for E/Q (ellinit output), returning [u,v] power series (variable x=exp(2iπz)) with d terms. Assumes E is a strong Weil curve and Manin constant equals 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pullback of the Néron differential equals 2iπ f(z) dz where f(x)=∑_{n>0} ellan(E,n) x^n. Library syntax: GEN elltaniyama(GEN E, long precdl).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltatepairing: Tate pairing requires m-torsion for P
rubrics_metrics.description: elltatepairing(E,P,Q,m) computes the Tate pairing of P and Q on E; P must be of m-torsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN elltatepairing(GEN E, GEN P, GEN Q, GEN m).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltors: torsion subgroup format and generators
rubrics_metrics.description: elltors(E) returns the torsion subgroup of E as [t, v1, v2] where t is order, v1 describes structure as product of cyclic groups, and v2 gives generators for these cyclic groups. E may be over a number field or finite field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: elltors(ellinit([-1,0])) returns [4,[2,2],[[0,0],[1,0]]] indicating Z/2×Z/2 with listed generators. Library syntax: GEN elltors(GEN E).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltwist: quadratic twist construction and usage
rubrics_metrics.description: elltwist(E,{P}) returns coefficients [a1,a2,a3,a4,a6] of the twist of elliptic curve E by quadratic extension defined by P (polynomial) or quadpoly(P) when P is integer. Over finite fields P can be omitted to get random non-trivial twist. For number fields, replace by minimal model if exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include twist by discriminant -3 and Artin–Schreier twists in characteristic 2. Library syntax: GEN elltwist(GEN E, GEN P = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellweilcurve: identify Weil curve and Smith invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: ellweilcurve(E,{&ms}) returns [vE,vS] where vE contains minimal models for curves isogenous to E and vS lists Smith invariants for lattices L_E in L_f. The strong Weil curve among isogenous curves is the one with Smith invariants [c,c] (c the Manin constant, conjecturally 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If optional ms provided, it should be msfromell(E,0) output; routine allows identification of strong Weil curve. Examples show finding index n with vS[n]==[1,1]. Library syntax: GEN ellweilcurve(GEN E, GEN *ms = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellweilpairing: Weil pairing of m-torsion points
rubrics_metrics.description: ellweilpairing(E,P,Q,m) computes the Weil pairing of points P and Q of m-torsion on E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN ellweilpairing(GEN E, GEN P, GEN Q, GEN m).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellwp: Weierstrass ℘ function and optional derivative
rubrics_metrics.description: ellwp(w,{z=x},{flag=0}) computes ℘(z) attached to lattice w (from ellperiods or ellinit). If flag=1 returns [℘(z), ℘'(z)]. Can also compute series expansion around z=0 and accepts E as input where w=E.omega.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series expansion via ellwp(E) or ellwp(E, x+O(x^k)). GEN ellwp0 and ellwpseries are also available for different argument types and series outputs. Library syntaxes: GEN ellwp0(GEN w, GEN z = NULL, long flag, long prec) and GEN ellwp(GEN w, GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellxn: division polynomials giving numerator/denominator of [n]P abscissa
rubrics_metrics.description: ellxn(E,n,{v=x}) returns [φ_n(P), ψ_n(P)^2] polynomials that give numerator and denominator of the x-coordinate of [n]P (in standard notation [n]P = (φ_n ψ_n : ω_n : ψ_n^3)). The returned pair depends only on v (the abscissa variable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for algebraic manipulation of multiples. Example shows computing ellxn(E,2,'X) then substituting P[1] to recover x-coordinate of 2P. Library syntax: GEN ellxn(GEN E, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellzeta: Weierstrass ζ function, quasi-periods and series
rubrics_metrics.description: ellzeta(w,{z=x}) computes ζ(z,L) attached to lattice w (via ellperiods). Quasi-periods η_i are obtained as 2 ζ(ω_i/2). Series expansion around z=0 is supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasi-periods useful for values at non-small z. Optional precision and default series precision behavior described. Library syntax: GEN ellzeta(GEN w, GEN z = NULL, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellztopoint: map parameter z back to curve point; cases
rubrics_metrics.description: ellztopoint(E,z) computes [x,y] on E corresponding to complex or p-adic parameter z (inverse of ellpointtoz). For p-adic multiplicative reduction z is treated as element on Tate curve Q_p^*/q^Z; for complex numbers x=℘(z)-b2/12 and y=℘'(z)/2 - (a1 x + a3)/2. z in lattice gives point at infinity [0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior differs for split vs non-split multiplicative reduction (use E.tate). Examples show p-adic output with O(p^n) terms. Library syntax: GEN pointell(GEN E, GEN z, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: genus2red: reduction type and conductor for genus 2 curves (output format and caveats)
rubrics_metrics.description: genus2red(PQ,{p}) determines reduction at p>2 of genus 2 curve C/Q given by y^2=P(x) or y^2+Q(x)y=P(x). Returns [N, FaN, T, V] where N is local or global conductor, FaN its factorization, T a minimal integral model y^2=T over Z[1/2], and V describes reduction types at considered primes. If p omitted determines reduction for all odd primes dividing discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CAVEAT: interface may change; program incomplete for p=2 (may return odd part of conductor only). The V vector format for local p is [p, stable, red], with stable = [type, vecj] and type in {1..7} indicating classification (1: smooth/pot. good; 2: elliptic+node; 3: P^1 with two nodes; 4: union of two P^1 crossing at 3 points; 5: union of two elliptic curves; 6,7: elliptic+P^1 or two singular components). red = [NUtype, neron] uses Namikawa–Ueno symbols and gives Néron component group as finite abelian group. Notes explain ordering and normalizations of Kodaira/Namikawa-Ueno symbols. Library syntax: GEN genus2red(GEN PQ, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperellcharpoly: Frobenius characteristic polynomial for hyperelliptic curves
rubrics_metrics.description: hyperellcharpoly(X) returns characteristic polynomial of Frobenius automorphism for a non-singular hyperelliptic curve X over a finite field, given by P (y^2=P(x)) or [P,Q] (y^2+Qy=P with Q^2+4P squarefree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This polynomial is the numerator of zeta-function and is useful for point counts and further arithmetic. Library syntax: GEN hyperellcharpoly(GEN X).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperellpadicfrobenius: Frobenius on crystalline module for hyperelliptic curves
rubrics_metrics.description: hyperellpadicfrobenius(Q,p,n) returns matrix of Frobenius endomorphism ϕ on crystalline module D_p(X)=Q_p ⊗ H^1_dR(X/Q) with respect to basis (ω, xω, ..., x^{g-1}ω), computed to absolute p-adic precision p^n. Requires p ≥ d and X has good reduction at p (d=deg Q with d=2g+1 or 2g+2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The characteristic polynomial of ϕ equals numerator of zeta-function of reduction of X modulo p. Library syntax: GEN hyperellpadicfrobenius(GEN Q, ulong p, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: hyperellratpoints: rational points on hyperelliptic curves up to height with flexible h parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: hyperellratpoints(X,h,{flag=0}) returns affine rational points on integral model X of naive height less than h. Flag=1 stops early. X given by P or [P,Q] as in hyperellcharpoly. Parameter h can be integer H (max(|n|,d)<H), or vector [N,D], or [N,[D1,D2]] to restrict numerators and denominators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors ellratpoints but for hyperelliptic curves; choose h format depending on search strategy. Library syntax: GEN hyperellratpoints(GEN X, GEN h, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: L-function definition: three required axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: An L-function datum (a, a*, A, N, k, ε, r) defines an L-function L(a,s) if it satisfies: (1) Convergence: coefficients a_n have polynomial growth so series converges in some right half-plane; (2) Analytic continuation: L(s) meromorphically continues to C with finitely many poles; (3) Functional equation: there exists integer k, complex ε (usually |ε|=1) and associated a* giving Λ(a,k-s)=ε Λ(a*,s) for completed Λ functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume multiplicativity/Euler product. For many number-theory applications a*=a (self-dual) but not required. The implementation stores redundant data to speed computations and expects implied constants in the O() to be small; numerical results are experimental and precision must be increased to verify. The L-function package is for experimentation rather than proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta function via Mellin inversion and functional equation
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an L-function with completed Λ, define θ(a,t) := (1/2πi) ∫_{(c)} t^{-s} Λ(s) ds (Mellin inversion) and equivalently θ(a,t)=∑_n a_n K(n t / N^{1/2}) where K involves γ_A. The functional equation for Λ translates into θ(a,1/t) - ε t^k θ(a*,t) = P_Λ(t) (polynomial from polar part).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: θ(t) is analytic in a cone and often easier to compute than L(s); use this to infer missing invariants. Compute K and θ via lfun package routines; the polar part introduces polynomial/log terms only when poles are present. Use theta routines for efficient numerical evaluation when many values needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data structures for L-functions: Lmath, Ldata, Linit and precision considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Three levels: Lmath (mathematical description), Ldata (computational description containing (a,a*,A,k,N,ε,r)), and Linit (Ldata plus precomputations for fast numerical evaluation over a domain and requested accuracy). L-functions routines accept any of these as first argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide exact components where possible; the implementation assumes implied constants in O() are small. For many evaluations construct an Linit once and reuse; warnings are issued if used outside initialized domain. Precision is specified in bits (realbitprecision) rather than decimal digits—use realbitprecision to control runtimes finely; realprecision increases by 64-bit chunks. The package is intended for experimentation and conjecture formulation, not formal proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: lfun initialization and use: performance and precision advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct Linit via lfuninit(Linit範,domain) to compute many values efficiently (e.g., zeros, plots). lfuncreate constructs basic Ldata from minimal information. Precision choices strongly affect runtime; most lfun routines request precision in bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Z = lfuncreate(1) for Riemann zeta; L = lfuninit(Z,[1/2,0,100]) to evaluate ζ(1/2+it) for |t|<100. Reinitialize Linit if used outside its domain (inefficient). Increase realbitprecision to improve accuracy and verify numeric stability.
